nodes.name: Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: For a typical synthesis of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2, 3.76 g of glycine and 3.66 ml of concentrated HCl were added to ethylene glycol (450 ml) with ultrapure water (50 ml) and ultrasonically dispersed to form a buffer solution, followed by the addition of rGO (50 mg), SnCl4 (5 mmol), and antimony precursor. The mixture was heated to 70°C for 24 h with magnetic agitation. Subsequently, the resulting suspension was washed by centrifugation with ultrapure water, and was then freeze-dried for 48 h. Finally, Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 was obtained by calcining the obtained powder in air at 650°C for 2 h to remove the rGO template.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows the Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 catalyst contains 10.5 wt% Sn and 89.5 wt% Sb.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma spectroscopy indicates that the as-prepared Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 catalyst contains 10.5 wt% tin and 89.5 wt% antimony.

nodes.characterization_summary: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 matches well with that of SnO2, demonstrating that antimony atoms were successfully incorporated into SnO2 to form solid solutions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Supplementary Fig. 12) of Turing Sb 0.1 Sn 0.9 O 2 matches well with that of SnO 2 , demonstrating that antimony atoms were successfully incorporated into SnO 2 to form solid solutions.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals holey 2D nanosheet morphology of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 with specific surface area of 66.28 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Fig. 1a,b) of the Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 catalyst show the morphology of holey 2D nanosheets with a specific surface area of 66.28 m² g⁻¹ (Supplementary Fig. 13).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows the Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 catalyst is composed of multiple chains around 5 nm in diameter with various orientations, interconnected to create a continuous network with plenty of grain boundaries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) (Fig. 1c), the Turing S b 0.1 S n 0.9 O 2 catalyst is composed of multiple chains around 5 nm in diameter with various orientations...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image clearly shows a number of grain boundaries with various crystallographic planes and orientations in Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2, in agreement with fast Fourier transform images.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image in Fig. 1d clearly shows a number of grain boundaries...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping and line scanning profiles verify the uniform distribution of tin and antimony in Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping (Fig. 1h) and line scanning profiles (Supplementary Fig. 14) verify the uniform distribution of tin and antimony...

nodes.characterization_summary: The thickness of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 is determined to be ~1.65 nm by atomic force microscopy, implying its ultrathin nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The thickness of Turing Sb 0.1 Sn 0.9 O 2 is determined to be ~1.65 nm by atomic force microscopy (Fig. 2a), implying its ultrathin nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 shows a stronger electron paramagnetic resonance intensity relative to other references, revealing its defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Turing Sb 0.1 Sn 0.9 O 2 shows a stronger electron paramagnetic resonance intensity relative to other references (Fig. 2b), revealing its defects...

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Sn 3d peaks and valence band of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 are downshifted compared to Turing SnO2, indicating electronic interaction from Sb incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS (Fig. 2c) and valence band (Fig. 2d) results illustrate that both the Sn 3d peak and the valence band of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 present downshifted peaks in comparison with those of Turing SnO2...

nodes.characterization_summary: Sn K-edge XANES shows higher white line peak and absorption edge for Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 than Turing SnO2, indicating slightly higher valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white line peak and the absorption edge of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 in XANES spectra (Fig. 2e) are slightly higher than those of Turing SnO2, revealing that the valence state of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 is slightly higher...

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed EXAFS shows Sn–O–Sn distance of Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 is 3.72 Å, slightly shorter than that of Turing SnO2 (3.73 Å), with low coordination numbers due to high-density defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the Fourier-transformed EXAFS spectra and corresponding fitting curve results (Fig. 2f and Supplementary Table 1)... the Sn–O–Sn distance of Turing Sb 0.1 Sn 0.9 O 2 is 3.72 Å...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS shows higher *OCHO coverage (~1400 cm⁻¹) on Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 at -0.9 V compared to SnO2, and higher OH stretching (~3600 cm⁻¹) indicating high oxophilicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coverage of the peak at ~1400 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 4a–c) associated with *OCHO intermediates over Turing Sb0.1Sn0.9O2 at relatively high overpotentials (-0.9 V) is close to that of Turing SnO2 and much higher than that of SnO2...
